reviews.review:
Pigeon's Mission reminds me of why I fell in love with gaming when I was a child. The controls are tight, the game is action packed and full of variety, and the art style is amazing. 

Gameplay - The game has a weapon system that is surprisingly deep. You collect seeds and use them as "universal energy" for all your guns, for healing, for your jetpack. The game looks like a simple platformer but it's actually about resource management. Picking the right tool for the job, prioritizing which enemies to take out first, and planning your route. It hides its depth and complexity behind the cute, childlike art style.

Controls - Tight, crisp controls and very responsive. It's a real joy to just move and traverse the world.

Variety - The game is jam packed with variety. It doesn't waste your time. It's tight, constantly introduces novelty, and it never gets stale. One moment you're jumping, the next moment you're flying, the next you're swimming and fighting swordfish, the next you hop on a roller coaster while dodging enemies. 

But looking at it as a whole, what it does for me specifically is that it makes me feel like a kid again. It has a childlike earnestness to it that I find unique and hard to find in today's gaming landscape. Many games try to be quirky or edgy, but Pigeon's Mission is simply trying to be itself. It has heart.

What a joy! Highly recommended.
